prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation. Layers (supervisory, bay execution, protection) separated; none silently substitutes another. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): sequencing, interlocks, timestamps; validates requests vs mode/interlocks/authority/availability; flags incomplete/contradictory ops; ages-out stale points to degraded; receives Breaker Inspection Tag (from Cinder) and Battery Load Test Record (from Station DC System); sends Bay Status Digest to Glasswing. North/South Bay Controllers: own bay only; North blocks close if interlocks not ready, keeps local control without supervisory comms; South reports mode/availability. Breaker Control Unit: executes accepted commands, returns position/health; tested only via commands that cannot bypass interlocks/authority. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): independent, trips without comms; sends Relay Diagnostic Note to Larkspur; testing must not remove coverage from energized feeder. North Protection Panel: zone trip paths network-independent. Transformer Protection Panel: transformer-only, reports abnormal. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): controls/indications with quality/stale status, no protection; retains cleared alarms; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; receives Protocol Retry Summary. Station Gateway: external boundary; rejects/logs malformed/stale/unauthorized requests; link errors never shown as equipment-state change; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): synchronized/degraded/unavailable; sends Clock Drift Snapshot to Orchard. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative time-tagged evidence incl. testing/restoration; flags uncertain times; retention/holds/backup. Maintenance Remote Terminal: authorized sessions, no interlock bypass; receives Settings Review Receipt. Station DC System: loss abnormal. Engineering Workstation: review only, changes via change control; produces Settings Review Receipt. Actors: Control Room Operator: procedural requests; switching to Keystone; produces Clearance Handoff Memo; reviews work packages/restrictions; tracks out-of-service protection until restored; treats remote indications unavailable when comms degraded. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): Isolation Boundary Card; confirms prerequisites, keeps switching sequence current, handback. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): settings, reviews test scope/restoration criteria. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): verifies identity, local indications, work boundaries; works only after clearance/isolation/grounding; reports unsafe/discrepancies. Substation Supervisor: authorization, change control (comms, mapping, logic), coordinates timing with Keystone. Requirements: local before

New part:
S218: A suspected controller or relay fault is assessed before any restart, bypass, or replacement is attempted.
S219: Restoration includes confirming normal indications, protection availability, communications status, and the removal of temporary test connections.
S220: The Substation Supervisor confirms that required records are complete and that operating restrictions are formally cleared before returning equipment to normal service.
S221: Operational assurance at Alder Creek depends on clear authority, verified equipment state, and records that support later review.
S222: The Control Room Operator remains responsible for deciding whether an automation request is appropriate for current operating conditions.
S223: The Bay Automation Controller shall execute only commands permitted by its approved logic and configured interlocks.
S224: The Feeder Protection Relay shall retain its protective function independently of supervisory communications.
S225: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection behavior after material changes and records any unresolved concerns for operational follow-up.
S226: The Station Supervisory Control System presents control indications and command results for operator assessment.
S227: The Sequence Event Archive retains time-ordered records needed to reconstruct significant control and protection events.
S228: The Engineering Workstation shall be used for authorized configuration work under established change control.
S229: The Satellite Time Receiver supports consistent event timing, and time-quality concerns shall be investigated before records are relied upon for sequence analysis.
S230: The Station Gateway shall maintain the defined boundary between station automation and external communications.
S231: The Station DC System shall be confirmed available before switching that depends on station control power.
S232: The Breaker Control Unit shall reject commands that do not satisfy its configured permissive conditions.
S233: Substation Field Crew uses the Isolation Boundary Card to verify the approved work boundary before entering the controlled area.
S234: Substation Field Crew reports unexpected equipment conditions promptly and pauses work when the approved boundary is uncertain.
S235: Switching Desk Coordinator receives the Clearance Handoff Memo and confirms that its clearance status agrees with the active switching record.
S236: Keystone shall confirm that switching authority, equipment state, and communication limits are understood before coordinating any automation-enabled action.
S237: The Substation Supervisor verifies that unresolved risks have an assigned owner and an agreed disposition before normal service is resumed.
S238: The Control Room Operator confirms indications locally when remote status is incomplete, inconsistent, or delayed.
S239: The Protection Relay Engineer assesses unexplained trips and abnormal protection indications before protection is returned to service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
